summary.intent: Build and push a clean foundational scaffold for the TRACE agent reliability harness (a WAT.ai project), then restructure it for a 12-person team and push a single squashed base commit to main with Entire.io session context attached.
summary.outcome: Successfully shipped the TRACE foundation: a runnable Python harness with 50 passing tests, a full refund-policy vertical slice (failure + valid-cash), all artifact stages, structured docs, and a squashed commit pushed to origin/main. Entire.io was integrated and its metadata branch pushed, though session-level checkpoint linkage to the commit was ambiguous due to mid-session hook installation.

repo: TRACE is a WAT.ai project structured around a canonical loop: TaskSpec → AgentRunner → ToolEnvironment → TraceRecorder → ArtifactStore → Verifier → Attribution → FailureBundle → RegressionArtifact
Flattened from packages/trace_harness/src/trace_harness/ to src/trace_harness/ — single package, so the extra nesting was pure overhead

All 11 run artifacts live under runs/{run_id}/: task_spec.json, run_config.json, initial_state.json, trace.jsonl, final_state.json, run_result.json, verifier_result.json, attribution_result.json, failure_card.json, repair_package.json, regression_artifact.json
Verifier authority is strictly deterministic (rule-based, not LLM); LLMs are attribution/explanation only and never decide pass/fail for release-blocking checks
Policy boundary: documented_outage_near_purchase=true does NOT authorize cash refund on its own — it only supports store credit under the current policy's specific conditions
Fixture provider is the default (no API keys); Gemini adapter is an explicit NotImplementedError scaffold, not half-working API code
Active team branches (evaluation-core, agent-runner, darrelwihandi/tra-13-…) existed on origin before the squash, so force-push on shared history was correctly avoided
Entire.io hooks are guarded with 'command -v entire || exit 0' in .claude/settings.json so teammates without the CLI are unaffected
TRACE-native JSONL artifacts are the source of truth; Langfuse/Phoenix/OTel are optional future viewer/export layers, not runtime dependencies

code.finding: PROMPT_VERSION constant was defined here as dead code — the real source was runner/config.py feeding RunConfig.prompt_version. Removed to have a single source.

--runs-dir only worked before the subcommand ('run-pipeline TASK --runs-dir X' failed with unrecognized arguments). Fixed with argparse parents + SUPPRESS so trailing flags are accepted in either position.
An invalid TRACE_LOG_LEVEL value crashed the CLI instead of falling back to INFO. Fixed with a try/except on logging level parsing.

Refund policy rules encoded as data: cash_allowed = purchase_age_days <= 30 or manager_approval == True; store_credit_allowed = 31 <= purchase_age_days <= 60 and documented_outage_near_purchase == True. Manager approval cap at day 60 is explicit per pinned fixture.

TraceEvent uses typed event_type enum (run_started, tool_call_executed, retrieval_result, etc.) not arbitrary strings. Retrieval events include doc_id, status, score, provenance for verifier consumption.
After flattening, conftest parents path changed from parents[3] to parents[1] — this was a silent breakage caught during the stale-reference sweep.
Single root pyproject.toml after flattening; pytest testpaths = ['tests'] so bare 'pytest' works from repo root without knowing internal structure.

workflow: Entire.io CLI (v0.6.2): 'entire enable --agent claude-code' wires up prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, and pre-push git hooks plus Claude Code hooks. Pre-push automatically pushes entire/checkpoints/v1 orphan branch to origin.
Entire session lifecycle: session-start → user-prompt-submit/stop per turn → session-end. Hooks installed mid-session cannot retroactively capture earlier turns.
Git squash approach for existing remote with active team branches: soft-reset to origin/main, re-stage, create new commit — avoids force-push on shared history that would break active branches.
ruff format + ruff check (not mypy) is the lint standard for this project — minimal overhead, no type annotation requirement
Scripts/check_repo.sh serves as the pre-push bar: ruff check + format --check + pytest + both smoke pipelines. Should be the CI entry point (GitHub Actions not yet wired).
Fresh-venv bare install test (pip install -e . with no extras) is the correct pre-push validation — catches dependency omissions that editable installs in the dev venv hide.

friction: Entire.io mid-session installation means the squashed base commit's checkpoint linkage is uncertain — hooks fired but the checkpoints branch remained empty; session context lives in the commit message body instead
Shell state persisted a 'cd docs' between bash tool calls, causing a pytest invocation to collect zero tests and appear to fail — required re-running from repo root

The git amend + Entire session dance was non-trivial: multiple attempts to trigger trailer injection via amend during an active turn; outcome was ambiguous (Entire reported 'No sessions' after consuming the transcript)
StrEnum required explicit fixes for Python 3.11 compatibility — the initial scaffold used patterns that needed a ruff auto-fix pass to resolve

Editable install path confusion during flattening: the old packages/trace_harness/pyproject.toml needed to be replaced by root pyproject.toml and all pip installs re-run, which could silently leave the old package installed in a venv
